7. A female - male trans man who still has female p hysical characteristics may
identify strongly as a man but may request to be searched by a female constable. In
such a case, the trans man should still be referred to using male pronouns and
treated as a man in all other ways except in terms of the gender of the constable
who searches him.

8. A male - female trans woman who still has the ma le physical characteristics
may identify strongly as a woman but may request to be searched by a male
constable. In such a case the trans woman should still be referred to using female
pronouns and treated as a woman in all other ways except in terms of the gender of
the constable who searches her.
33

9. If a person is unwilling to make such an electio n, the constable should try and
determine the gender in which the person lives their life. This is likely to be indicated
by the name, title or gender on their main identity document e.g. drivers licence,
bank card etc. If the person appears for example to live as a woman, they should be
treated as such.
